title: The block appears in the picker and can be added
observed: Scratch card was available in Elements. Dragging it onto the first step created a covered card in the desktop and mobile canvas.

title: It can be placed on any step, including a success step
observed: Added cards to the first step, a new Blank Step, and Success. All three rendered. The temporary Success card was later removed through the builder.

title: The revealed offer takes rich text
observed: Entered “QA OFFER: Save 15% — View terms”, applied bold, and linked it to the test storefront’s #qa-offer anchor. Formatting and link survived publication.

title: Show the offer while editing
observed: The editing toggle exposed the offer and restored the cover when switched off. It did not discard offer content.

title: Prompt text can be set
observed: Typed and cleared the prompt. On the refreshed builder, “SCRATCH TO REVEAL YOUR SPECIAL OFFER” shrank to fit a 320px card. Empty text left the cover valid. Earlier stale-session clipping was superseded by this retest.

title: Cover colour can be set
observed: Selected a preset and committed custom hex #154E87. The refreshed builder and published card show blue-tinted foil.

title: Prompt text styles can be set
observed: Changed the prompt to the company font IBM Plex Mono, 24px, normal then bold weight, yellow #FFF176, and italic. The cover visibly applied all five settings. These controls appeared after refreshing the builder; the earlier missing-control observation was superseded.

title: Full width versus a fixed pixel width
observed: Fixed width exposed a pixel field; 320px narrowed the card. Returning to Full width removed that field and expanded the card. Verified on the refreshed builder.

title: Height and corner radius
observed: Set height to 160px and corner radius to 28px; both applied and persisted. Tabbing from the fixed-width field to Height kept the entered width and moved focus correctly.

title: Reveal threshold can be set
observed: Published 20% and 80% thresholds separately. The 20% card remained covered at 19.94% erased and began fading by 24.32%; the 80% card stayed covered at 79.94% and began fading by 84.32%. Sampling was between horizontal strokes. Final setting: 50%.

title: An action can be attached
observed: Cycled all available action types: Close form, Submit form, Go to URL, Do nothing, and Subscribe via text messaging. Relevant controls appeared and selections saved. Actual backend success is assessed separately under O07/O09/O18. SMS was configuration-only; no SMS was sent.

title: Reorder, duplicate and delete
observed: Reordered the temporary Success card and deleted it without leaving an orphan. No Duplicate control was available in the inspected block menu, so duplication was not verified.

title: Settings survive save and reopen
observed: Reopened the builder after saving. Prompt, rich offer/link, company font, 24px bold italic yellow text, blue cover, full width, 160px height, 28px radius, threshold and action were retained. Later low-threshold capture shows the retained style settings.

title: Publish
observed: Published successfully and confirmed the Live badge plus the actual card on the storefront. Nonblocking form alerts were present; publication completed.

title: Edit an already published card
observed: Republished the changed prompt and custom blue cover. Live prompt and RGB (21,78,135) were verified; 160px height, 28px radius, threshold and offer/link remained intact. Further style/threshold edits were separate test scenarios.

title: The card renders on the live form
observed: The latest published card rendered with blue foil and the configured prompt. Desktop canvas measured 428 × 160 CSS pixels; radius and font matched the builder.

title: Scratching reveals at roughly the threshold
observed: Real mouse strokes revealed near the configured threshold. Verified at 20%, 50%, and 80%; sampled reveal points were approximately 24%, 54%, and 84%, respectively. The cover stayed opaque immediately below each threshold.

title: A tap does not reveal
observed: A single stationary mouse click in the center of the cover revealed the entire offer. Before: 0% erased. After 700ms: cover removed. Reproduced in fresh sessions, including after refreshed assets. This conflicts with the expected no-reveal behavior for <6px travel.

title: Scratching erases properly
observed: A 55px short stroke cleared approximately 4.96% of the canvas to fully transparent pixels. Only a thin antialiased edge remained partially transparent.

title: Resizing mid-scratch does not restore the cover
observed: Scratched a partial region, then narrowed the viewport from 1440px to 390px. Visible card size changed from 428 × 160 to about 203.6 × 76.1px. Erased fraction stayed exactly 12.4927%; no restored cover. This sampled a partial scratch rather than exactly half.

title: The offer renders correctly once revealed
observed: Normal-motion reveal used opacity 0.32s ease-out, including an observed intermediate opacity, then removed the cover. The bold offer text and link remained visible.

title: A dwell-safe action fires after the offer is readable
observed: Submit-to-Preview-List-and-close was published and exercised with a synthetic example.com identity. Offer remained visible at 500ms; subscription POST began at 1,627ms. Subscription and analytics requests failed with net::ERR_FAILED/CORS, so successful list submission cannot be claimed.

title: A navigating action still navigates
observed: Published Go to URL and revealed the card. The browser navigated to the configured storefront URL with ?scratchqa=redirect.

title: A multi-step transition works
observed: Published Submit form → Preview List → Show next step. Reveal did not produce a verifiable next step within the observation window. The subscription request was blocked by CORS (missing Access-Control-Allow-Origin), so this is an end-to-end blocker rather than a proven scratch transition defect.

title: The card can be revealed without scratching
observed: Tab traversal reached the reveal control. Enter and Space each revealed the offer in independent checks. A focus outline was visible against the cover; no formal contrast-ratio audit was performed.

title: The offer becomes reachable after the reveal
observed: The offer link had tabindex=-1 while covered. After reveal that restriction was removed and the link received focus. Link destination and rich formatting were preserved.

title: A custom prompt font renders on the cover
observed: Published IBM Plex Mono Bold 700 for the prompt only. The browser loaded the 700 font face; canvas drawing font was italic bold 24px “IBM Plex Mono”, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif. Live screenshot visibly matches the selected font.

title: Touch scratching works
observed: Chrome mobile emulation accepted synthetic touch strokes and revealed the offer while scrollY stayed 0. A physical phone and real finger input were not available, so the full phone acceptance criterion remains unverified.

title: Rotation and narrow viewports
observed: Emulated 390×844 portrait, 844×390 landscape, and 320×640 narrow viewports. The full-width card resized and remained visible. This verifies responsive viewport behavior, not physical-device rotation.

title: Safari
observed: Desktop Safari and real iOS Safari were not exercised by this Chrome-based kit run. No Safari pass is inferred from Chrome emulation. Requires a Safari/iOS rerun of O01, O02, O06 and O07.

title: Firefox
observed: Installed and launched Firefox 155 in a fresh context. Shopify unlocked, but Klaviyo never initialized: the script tag existed, no Klaviyo response was observed, and the scratch card never appeared. Repeated attempts could not reach O01/O02/O06/O07. This is a browser/runtime blocker, with cause unresolved.

title: The cover fade respects the OS setting
observed: With reducedMotion=reduce, computed cover transition was none. On reveal the first sampled opacity was 0, followed by removal; no intermediate fade was sampled. This used browser emulation of the OS preference.

title: The submit is recorded
observed: Subscription and analytics requests failed. Preview List was checked afterwards: it still had one existing member dated before this run, and no synthetic QA submission. Attribution to this form was therefore not verified. The public capture intentionally excludes the existing profile’s details.
